answer: Each identity claims one terrace in a haven district and locks a 70-credit bond, then files a jade seal impression with the terrace step count and date. An auditor recounts the steps from the public terrace survey table for that haven and date, burning the bond on a count miss or a repeated seal serial. First terrace costs 31, the kth 31+6(k-1); the 1000th costs 6025, and 1000 fake terraces cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 at risk. A rented-seal ring fails because a seal serial files once per epoch; a second filing burns both bonds. An honest agent pays 31 once, bond back after a clean audit.
